problem: Embodied Question Answering has focused on indoor scenes; city-scale outdoor spaces (ambiguous similar objects, cross-scale actions, view-dependent perception) have no active-exploration EQA benchmark or agent, and existing outdoor QA (City-3DQA, EarthVQA) is passive.
motivation: Urban EQA matters for autonomous systems, urban profiling and city planning. Cities are vast and open, so indoor-style frontier or random exploration is inefficient, and questions must be disambiguated with landmarks and spatial relations.
key_idea: A hierarchical Planner-Manager-Actor LLM/VLM agent decomposes a city EQA question into navigation, exploration and collection sub-tasks, and executes them over an object-centric 2D grid cognitive map using landmark-based spatial relations.
insight: Ablations show the object-centric map is the most critical component (QAA 3.00 to 2.31 without it), and removing the navigator hurts more than removing the explorer, so landmark-based navigation is key in cities. VQA agents given the ground-truth view score 4.37, so the remaining gap is mostly about acquiring good views (exploration and view refinement) rather than about VLM perception. The Collector's fine-grained view adjustment improves QAA and NE with more steps.
method: Planner: GPT-4 with few-shot three-step CoT extracts objects and spatial relations, derives information requirements, and produces a plan of Navigation/Exploration/Collection sub-tasks with Known/Unknown object states.

Object-centric cognitive map: 400 m x 400 m grid at 1 m resolution centered on the start pose; GroundSAM segments landmarks, depth and pose give a point cloud that is projected to 2D grids, and adjacent or overlapping object grids are merged across time steps.
Memory and Process Control: store Req_info, Object_info and History, pick the next sub-task, and call zero-shot LLM Answer Generation from Req_info once the plan is done.
Navigator: takes a landmark and a direction (e.g. west of building_1), finds the nearest target point on the map and plans an A* path in 10 m segments, updating after each map update.

Explorer: Move-and-Look-Around; exploration points spaced 10 m apart in the region defined by landmark and relation, four views (front, back, left, right) per point, and a VLM checks whether the target is visible.
Collector: a GPT-4o VLA that answers the information requirement from the RGB view and picks one of nine fine-tuning actions (Move F/B/L/R/Up/Down, Turn L/R, KeepStill) for up to 10 steps.

CityEQA-EC benchmark: 443 raw human-annotated Q&A, expanded with landmarks and at least 4 initial poses within 200 m to 2,212 tasks, validated to 1,412 tasks in 6 categories on EmbodiedCity (UE4/AirSim); LLM-judge QAA scoring.

setting.action_space: UAV low-level moves: 10 m forward segments via A*, 30° turns, Collector adjustments (move/turn/up/down/keep still)
setting.privileged: none stated (agent pose is used to build the map)

numbers.eval_set_note: 200 tasks randomly selected from the 1,412 CityEQA-EC tasks (API limits)
numbers.extra: max 50 steps for navigation and exploration, 10 for collection; QAA on a 1-5 scale by LLM judge; MTS = mean time steps

numbers_note: CityEQA-EC has no official splits; the paper evaluates a random 200-task subset, so the split label 'val' is a placeholder. Human H-EQA reaches QAA 4.94, NE 38.72 and MTS 9.31 (a baseline, not included).
results: PMA reaches QAA 3.00, NE 46.56 m and MTS 24.44, which is 60.73% of human H-EQA accuracy. It beats the exploring baselines RE (2.19) and FBE (2.31) and the blind and Socratic agents (up to 2.82) while using far fewer steps than FBE (39.31). It remains well below humans (4.94) and the VQA-with-GT-view GPT-4o (4.37).
limitations: Only object-centric questions about static entities; dynamic events, crowds and temporal reasoning are not covered
Evaluated on only 200 tasks, in a single EmbodiedCity scene, with an LLM judge
Still much less efficient and accurate than humans, with error accumulation over long horizons and limited Collector view adjustments
